realism_constraints: No advanced forensic DNA analysis available
Photography and fingerprinting are established investigative tools
Quicklime is commonly believed to destroy bodies but actually preserves them
institution: Local police under Sergeant Cobbledick, assisted by Dr. John Thorndyke

cast.name: Angelina Frood (Peter "Jimmy" Bundy)
cast.private_secret: disguised as Mr. Bundy, faked death using skeleton
cast.motive_seed: escape abusive husband and start anew

surface_summary: Angelina Frood mysteriously disappears, and a skeleton dressed in her clothes is found buried in a city wall. The police suspect murder, but the body is unrecognizable and the husband is missing. A disguised figure named Mr. Bundy appears, complicating the investigation.
accepted_facts: Angelina Frood disappeared on the night of April 26th
A skeleton dressed in her clothes was found buried in the city wall
Nicholas Frood, her husband, died earlier and was identified posthumously
Mr. Bundy is a person who appeared in Rochester shortly after Angelina's disappearance
inferred_conclusions: The skeleton is Angelina Frood's body
Nicholas Frood is the prime suspect for murder
Mr. Bundy is an unrelated man impersonating someone else
mechanism_description: Angelina Frood faked her disappearance and death by purchasing an ancient skeleton from a dealer and dressing it in her clothes to bury it in the city wall, creating the illusion of her death. She disguised herself as Mr. Bundy, a man with feminine features, to live undetected in Rochester. The real Nicholas Frood died earlier from a cocaine overdose, removing him from suspicion. Dr. Thorndyke uncovered the deception through photographic comparison, fingerprint analysis, and forensic evidence.
delivery_path: Angelina buys an ancient female skeleton from a dealer in London
She dresses the skeleton in her own clothes and accessories
The skeleton is buried in a prepared patch of the city wall
Angelina disguises herself as Mr. Bundy with a wig, makeup, and male clothing
She maintains the disguise while interacting with acquaintances and investigators
Dr. Thorndyke obtains photographs and fingerprints to compare Bundy and Angelina
The deception is revealed at the inquest when Angelina appears in person
outcome_result: Angelina Frood is revealed to be alive and disguised as Mr. Bundy, having faked her death with a skeleton, and the real Nicholas Frood was already dead.

false_assumption.statement: The skeleton found in the city wall is the actual body of Angelina Frood.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The skeleton was found dressed in Angelina's clothes and jewelry, and the disappearance of Angelina coincided with the discovery. The presence of personal effects and the skeleton's location strongly suggested it was her body.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals that the skeleton was an ancient specimen purchased and planted by Angelina herself to fake her death, while she lived disguised as Mr. Bundy.

supporting_points: He was known to be violent and addicted to drugs
He was searching for Angelina and had threatened her life
He carried a sheath-knife and had a motive of jealousy
He disappeared suspiciously around the time of Angelina's disappearance
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Nicholas Frood died before Angelina's disappearance and could not have committed the crime.

red_herrings.description: A man with a mole on his nose pawned Angelina's brooch, suggesting a suspicious character.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: An unknown local man possibly involved in the crime
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The man likely found the brooch and pawned it without involvement in the crime.

red_herrings.description: The disappearance of the gate key to the city wall patch where the skeleton was found.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Someone with access to the wall area, possibly the murderer
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The key was lost or taken as a prank and thrown over the fence, unrelated to the crime.

closed_circle.rationale: All key persons connected to the disappearance and investigation were local and had access or motive; no outsiders were involved.

time_windows: Night of April 26th to early May for disappearance and planting skeleton
Three months until July for body preservation and discovery

inference_path.observation: Skeleton found buried in city wall with personal effects of Angelina Frood
inference_path.correction: The skeleton was ancient and purchased, not Angelina's real body
inference_path.effect: Disproves that Angelina is dead and body in wall is hers
required_evidence: Bill from Oscar Hammerstein for purchase of skeleton dated April 19th
Photographic comparison of Mr. Bundy and Angelina Frood

inference_path.observation: Mr. Bundy appears as a man with masculine clothing and manner
inference_path.correction: Mr. Bundy is actually Angelina Frood in disguise
inference_path.effect: Explains the presence of 'Mr. Bundy' and faked disappearance
required_evidence: Fingerprints on tumbler and bottle matching Angelina Frood
Photographic composites and expert testimony by Dr. Thorndyke

inference_path.observation: Nicholas Frood is missing and suspected of murder
inference_path.correction: Nicholas Frood died earlier from cocaine overdose
inference_path.effect: Removes Nicholas Frood as suspect in Angelina's disappearance
required_evidence: Identification of Nicholas Frood's body at St. Barnabas hospital
Witness testimony of landlady and Dr. Strangeways

inference_path.observation: Quicklime burial believed to destroy bodies
inference_path.correction: Quicklime preserves bodies by drying, not destroying
inference_path.effect: Skeleton in wall could not be recent and is not Angelina's
required_evidence: Experiments by Mr. A. Lucas and Dr. Thorndyke on quicklime effects

inference_path.observation: Clues found progressively up the river and lane
inference_path.correction: Clues were deliberately planted to mislead investigators
inference_path.effect: Supports theory of staged disappearance and deception
required_evidence: Map of find locations from brooch to gate key
Testimony of Sergeant Cobbledick and Dr. Thorndyke

inference_path.observation: Fingerprints on household objects match Angelina Frood
inference_path.correction: Confirms that Angelina was present in the house disguised
inference_path.effect: Supports identity of Mr. Bundy as Angelina Frood
required_evidence: Photographs of fingerprints on tumbler, bottle, and kitchen objects

inference_path.observation: Mr. Bundy and Angelina Frood never seen together
inference_path.correction: They are the same person using disguise and deception
inference_path.effect: Explains how the deception was maintained
required_evidence: Testimony of Dr. Strangeways and photographic evidence
Expert testimony on disguise and personation

discriminating_test.design: Dr. Thorndyke and Dr. Strangeways visited Angelina's house to powder and photograph fingerprints on objects she had touched, including a tumbler and water bottle. They compared these prints with those found on photographs of Mr. Bundy, revealing identity. Photographic composites were created to compare facial features of Bundy and Angelina, confirming they were the same person.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test revealed that Mr. Bundy was actually Angelina Frood in disguise, proving the personation and faked death.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Matching fingerprints and photographic facial features conclusively demonstrate the identity of Mr. Bundy as Angelina Frood.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with detailed descriptions of the characters, their appearances, and behaviors, including the physical peculiarities of Mr. Bundy and Angelina Frood. The narrative includes detailed accounts of the photographic and fingerprint evidence, as well as the discovery of the skeleton and the key. The clues are all presented openly, allowing an attentive reader to deduce the deception and the true identity of Mr. Bundy before the final reveal.
